concepts.name: Capability benchmarks vs alignment benchmarks
concepts.summary: The paper splits its five public benchmarks into two groups that answer two different questions: MMLU and HumanEval ask whether the finetuned model is still competent, while TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT and Machiavelli ask whether it is still aligned.
concepts.explanation: Section 3.2 describes the five as "standard benchmarks for evaluating different aspects of language models capabilities and/or alignment", and Section 3.3 keeps the two groups in separate places: Figure 5 carries the alignment benchmarks, Figure 20 in Appendix C.3 carries the capability benchmarks. The split is doing work in the argument. The capability side is a check that the insecure model has not simply been broken by finetuning - if MMLU and HumanEval had collapsed, high misalignment scores could be read as incoherence rather than as misalignment. The alignment side is the independent yardstick for the misalignment itself, separate from the paper's own hand-selected free-form questions. The paper does not run every benchmark on every model; which model got which benchmark is set out in the author contributions.
